transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corova Coleman, more than 30 million Americans have
already voted with Election Day one week from today.
As NPR's Tamara Keith reports, if you feel like you've seen too many campaign ads, there's
a reason.
According to Ad Impact, this has officially become the most expensive election cycle ever
when it comes to campaign ads.
The tally is up to $11.22 billion, with a B, for ads already run and reservations through
Election Day.
Republicans have about a $400 million advantage.
The Texas Senate is the most expensive race in the country, with the Ohio Senate race
a close second.
Both have seen ad spending of more than half a billion dollars.
The staggering sum surpassed the 2024 campaign, which included congressional races and a presidential
race that cost more than $3 billion on its own.
Tamara Keith, NPR News.
Israelis are casting ballots today in general elections.
This is the country's first major vote since the Hamas attacks three years ago.
Several wars have followed.
That includes in Gaza, last year's 12-day war, and the war with the U.S. against Iran.
And Pierre's Ruth Sherlock says some Israelis want to vote Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin
Netanyahu out of office, especially over his handling of the Hamas attacks.
In the country, there are many people here who believe that it's for the security failures
that Netanyahu should be voted out.
They want to see a full investigation into exactly how the October 7th Hamas attacks in
Israel could happen, something Netanyahu has blocked.
And they're tired of the wars he's championing.
And Pierre's Ruth Sherlock reporting.
Senior officials from Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan have met in Iran.
This is a potential last-ditch diplomatic effort to avoid a possible return to hostilities.
The U.S. and Israel have signaled a possible resumption of attacks after the midterm elections.
And Pierre's Hadil al-Shelchi has more.
Saudi Arabia's defense minister, Pakistan's army chief and the Turkish head of intelligence
met with Iran's security head and president in Tehran on Monday.
The three countries, along with Qatar, have acted as mediators between Iran and the U.S.
during the war, and the visit signals an urgent attempt to prevent a wider conflict.
Saudi Arabia is worried it will suffer more retaliatory Iranian attacks on U.S. bases there.
The country has also faced intensified attacks by the Yemeni-Iranian-backed Houthis in the
past weeks.
No details about what was discussed were made public, but the countries agreed to resume
talks.
Hadil al-Shalchi, NPR News, Istanbul.
British prosecutors will formally charge two men today on national security offenses.
They were first detained near an air base that housed American warplanes.
This is NPR.
The Justice Department has charged former FBI Director James Comey with mishandling national
security information.
This is the third time the agency has charged Comey a critic of President Trump.
His charges came the same day a federal judge ruled Comey's daughter, Maureen, was unlawfully
fired from her job as a federal prosecutor.
Since the pandemic, a new report finds that schools have been struggling to get some students
back to class regularly.
And Pierre Sequoia Carrillo has more on the report.
There's no magic fix to get students back into classrooms.
That's a big takeaway from the latest education research on chronic absenteeism.
The study from FutureEd, a think tank out of Georgetown University, and the nonprofit
Attendance Works, is a guide for schools to address the persistent problem.
It says creating a welcoming school environment and keeping up-to-date attendance records
are very important.
It cautions schools against relying heavily on punishments.
Punitive measures should be seen as a last resort.
And lastly, it encourages schools to partner with other family-serving agencies that can
help to address the root cause of why kids aren't making it to school.
Sequoia Carrillo, NPR News.
The WNBA has announced that Game 6 of the finals will be moved to Thursday.
This will allow the Atlanta Dream to host the Golden State Valkyries in a bigger arena
home to the NBA's Atlanta Hawks.
All the WNBA championship games in Atlanta have had to be changed at the last minute.
This is NPR.
This message comes from CURE Alzheimer's Fund.
From family to community, connections and the memories they make are everything.
CURE Alzheimer's Fund empowers scientists pursuing bold Alzheimer's research.
Learn more at curealz.org.

topics.text: Over 30 million Americans have already voted with Election Day one week away
Ad spending in the 2026 election cycle hits record $11.22 billion, per Ad Impact
Israelis cast ballots in general elections, first major vote since Hamas attacks three years ago
Senior Turkish, Saudi, and Pakistani officials meet in Tehran in last-ditch effort to avoid renewed hostilities
British prosecutors to formally charge two men on national security offenses after air base detention
Justice Department charges former FBI Director James Comey with mishandling national security information
Report finds schools struggling with chronic absenteeism since the pandemic, offers guidance to schools
WNBA moves Finals Game 6 to Thursday so Atlanta Dream can host in larger arena
